title: Merchandise Displayers and Window Trimmers
description: Plan and erect commercial displays, such as those in windows and interiors of retail stores and at trade exhibitions.

tasks.text: Attend training sessions or corporate planning meetings to obtain new ideas for product launches.
Plan commercial displays to entice and appeal to customers.
Develop ideas or plans for merchandise displays or window decorations.
Select themes, lighting, colors, or props to be used.
Use computers to produce signage.
Prepare sketches, floor plans, or models of proposed displays.
Dress mannequins for displays.
Arrange properties, furniture, merchandise, backdrops, or other accessories, as shown in prepared sketches.
Change or rotate window displays, interior display areas, or signage to reflect changes in inventory or promotion.
Place prices or descriptive signs on backdrops, fixtures, merchandise, or floor.
Assemble or set up displays, furniture, or products in store space, using colors, lights, pictures, or other accessories to display the product.
Store, pack, and maintain inventory records of props, products, or display items.
Install booths, exhibits, displays, carpets, or drapes, as guided by floor plan of building or specifications.
Install decorations, such as flags, banners, festive lights, or bunting on or in building, street, exhibit hall, or booth.
Construct or assemble displays or display components from fabric, glass, paper, or plastic, using hand tools or woodworking power tools, according to specifications.
Take photographs of displays or signage.
Cut out designs on cardboard, hardboard, or plywood, according to motif of event.
Consult with store managers, buyers, sales associates, housekeeping staff, or engineering staff to determine appropriate placement of displays or products.
Maintain props, products, or mannequins, inspecting them for imperfections, doing touch-ups, cleaning up after customers, or applying preservative coatings as necessary.
Supervise or train staff members on daily tasks, such as visual merchandising.
Consult with advertising or sales staff to determine type of merchandise to be featured and time and place for each display.
Instruct sales staff in color coordination of clothing racks or counter displays.
Collaborate with others to obtain products or other display items.
Obtain plans from display designers or display managers and discuss their implementation with clients or supervisors.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Graphics software, SmugMug Flickr.

skills.name: Internet browser software
skills.def: Software to view the contents of web pages and to navigate from one page to another. Examples: Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge, Microsoft Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Google Docs, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, IBM Lotus Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat.
